edges.reason: Tens-and-ones composition includes the meaning of a teen number as one ten and units. This overlapping place-value content is necessary without prescribing the historical order of lessons.
Borrowing in general two-digit subtraction includes teen-minus-two-through-five subtractions in the units stage.
The target requires checking by addition, but it does not require the verification itself to use a column algorithm. Mental addition is a valid check.
edges.scope: Checking a written subtraction using a written column-addition verification

edges.reason: Written regrouping subtraction uses the same ten-for-ten-ones exchange explicitly named in the oral-subtraction endpoint. Direct instruction in the column layout does not eliminate that content, while prior mental subtraction fluency is outside this strict scope.
edges.scope: The base-ten borrowing meaning when one ten is exchanged for ten ones in written subtraction

edges.reason: Formal part/whole equations support selecting operations. An action model that joins groups and removes objects also identifies the two steps without separately naming the formal part/whole relation.
Column addition reinforces place-value alignment and regrouping. Mental hundreds/tens sums can be obtained by decomposition and unit counts without laying out written columns.
Mental arithmetic on hundreds and tens uses the values of those places in three-digit numbers.
